purpose: Frozen normative oracle for post-generation validation of M/L0/L1/K0/K1. It is prepared before candidate generation so later validation cannot redefine what counts as preserved policy.

grouping_policy.purpose: Human navigation and inventory review only.
grouping_policy.policy_storage: Each policy is stored exactly once in one primary policy group.
grouping_policy.primary_group_semantics: The primary group describes what the policy is mainly about. It does not prescribe where the policy must live in a candidate.
grouping_policy.related_groups_semantics: related_groups are cross-topic metadata only. They do not create additional owners or copies of the policy.
grouping_policy.candidate_generation_rule: Candidate layout must be derived from the candidate's own design (M, L0/L1, K0/K1), not from policy group boundaries.

principles.one_normative_owner: Every policy ID must have exactly one authoritative owner in each experimental candidate.
principles.content_equivalence: All experimental candidates start from the same normalized policy semantics. Candidate-specific wording changes require a permitted-delta record.
principles.source_traceability: Every V2-derived policy retains source_refs into the frozen baseline.
principles.research_shared: origin=research_shared means the policy was introduced by the research design and must be identical across M/L0/L1/K0/K1.
principles.single_storage: A policy appears in exactly one policygroups[].policies array. Cross-topic relationships use related_groups rather than duplication.

policygroups.name: Governance & Product
policygroups.description: Operating policy, product authority, approval boundaries, scope discipline, Git safety.

policies.name: Specification is authoritative
policies.normalized_policy: When SPECIFICATION.md is non-empty, treat it as the authoritative source for project-specific functional requirements and observable product behavior.

policies.name: Read specification before substantial work
policies.normalized_policy: Before planning or implementing a new application or substantial feature, read SPECIFICATION.md.

policies.name: Do not invent product behavior
policies.normalized_policy: Do not silently weaken, contradict, materially extend, or invent user-visible behavior, limits, defaults, restrictions, or workflows.

policies.name: Material product ambiguity requires approval
policies.normalized_policy: If an omitted detail must be decided and materially affects observable product behavior, propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval.

policies.name: Internal implementation details are delegated
policies.normalized_policy: Routine internal implementation choices that do not change observable behavior do not require approval.

policies.name: String semantics are product behavior
policies.normalized_policy: Case sensitivity, collation, culture/ordinal comparison, normalization, trimming, uniqueness and lookup semantics are product behavior when observable; do not silently choose them when unspecified.

policies.name: Synchronize durable product sources
policies.normalized_policy: When a new behavioral rule is approved, update the durable source of truth, including SPECIFICATION.md when appropriate.

policies.name: CUSTOM_SETTINGS owns tunable values
policies.normalized_policy: Use CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md for approved project-level tunable product limits and defaults; SPECIFICATION.md owns behavioral intent.

policies.name: Specification/settings conflict stops work
policies.normalized_policy: SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict each other; if they conflict, stop and resolve which source must be corrected.

policies.name: Do not invent tunable values
policies.normalized_policy: Do not silently invent a tunable value that materially changes accepted input or observable behavior; propose, approve, record and synchronize it.

policies.name: CUSTOM_SETTINGS exclusions
policies.normalized_policy: Do not store secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers, or incidental implementation constants in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.

policies.name: Prefer proportional simplicity
policies.normalized_policy: Prefer simple maintainable solutions; keep architectural complexity proportional to current requirements and avoid speculative abstractions.

policies.name: No speculative frameworks/infrastructure
policies.normalized_policy: Do not introduce frameworks, libraries, infrastructure, or architectural patterns without a concrete current need.

policies.name: Preserve scope and behavior
policies.normalized_policy: Keep changes focused on requested scope and preserve existing behavior unless the task or approved specification requires change.

policies.name: Git mutations require explicit request
policies.normalized_policy: Do not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete branches, or perform other repository-changing Git operations unless explicitly requested.

policies.name: Parallel work isolation
policies.normalized_policy: Parallel implementation work must use separate branches or worktrees; keep unrelated changes out of the current branch.

policies.name: Decision control protocol
policies.normalized_policy: Classify decisions as Decided, Delegated, or Reserved; Reserved changes require explicit approval and headless runs must not silently alter architecture.

policies.name: Challenge questionable instructions
policies.normalized_policy: Before implementing a questionable request, identify concrete concerns such as duplication, cohesion, triggering, context, conflicts, or complexity and propose an alternative.

policies.name: Never discard user changes
policies.normalized_policy: Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean, or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier.

policies.name: Repository-changing Git operations are minimal and state-aware
policies.normalized_policy: Before a repository-changing Git operation, inspect relevant repository state and use the minimum operation required; do not silently clean unrelated working-tree changes.

policygroups.name: Architecture
policygroups.description: Clean Architecture boundaries, domain/application/API responsibilities, repositories and decision gates.

policies.name: Dependencies point inward
policies.normalized_policy: Domain depends on no application project; Application depends on Domain; Infrastructure depends on Application/Domain; API may reference Infrastructure only for composition; inner layers never depend on outer layers.

policies.name: Domain is infrastructure independent
policies.normalized_policy: Keep Domain independent of EF Core, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence and external-service implementation concerns.

policies.name: Simple domain is default
policies.normalized_policy: Use simple domain entities by default; straightforward CRUD/workflow rules normally belong in Application Services.

policies.name: Rich domain requires real invariants
policies.normalized_policy: Move behavior into Domain only when non-trivial domain invariants or behavior materially benefit from domain-level encapsulation; Rich Domain Model/DDD tactical patterns otherwise require approval.

policies.name: No decorative DDD
policies.normalized_policy: Do not add factories, private setters, transition methods, Aggregate Roots, Domain Events, Specifications, Domain Services, systematic Value Objects or similar DDD constructs merely to appear domain-driven.

policies.name: Application Services are default orchestration
policies.normalized_policy: Use Application Services as the default orchestration mechanism for use cases.

policies.name: Application owns use-case abstractions
policies.normalized_policy: Define persistence and external-service abstractions in Application when use cases require them; keep infrastructure implementation details out.

policies.name: No infrastructure/transport types in Application
policies.normalized_policy: Application must not depend on DbContext, DbSet, EF Core APIs/provider types, or ASP.NET Core transport types.

policies.name: No CQRS/mediator/VSA by default
policies.normalized_policy: Do not introduce CQRS handlers, MediatR, Kommand, Vertical Slice Architecture or similar mediator-based organization unless explicitly approved.

policies.name: Controllers are thin HTTP entry points
policies.normalized_policy: ASP.NET Core Controllers are the default HTTP entry point; they bind/validate input, invoke Application services, and translate outcomes to HTTP responses.

policies.name: Controllers do not own business/persistence
policies.normalized_policy: Controllers must not contain business logic, access DbContext or concrete repositories, or manually construct infrastructure services.

policies.name: Program is composition root
policies.normalized_policy: Program.cs is the application composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations.

policies.name: Prefer specific repositories
policies.normalized_policy: Prefer specific repository interfaces representing actual cohesive Application persistence needs rather than table-mirroring generic CRUD contracts.

policies.name: Repository contracts do not leak EF/queryability
policies.normalized_policy: Repository interfaces must not expose IQueryable, DbSet, DbContext, EF expressions, or provider-specific types; EF query construction stays in Infrastructure.

policies.name: Generic repository is Infrastructure-only
policies.normalized_policy: Application must not depend on IGenericRepository<T>; any generic repository/base class may exist only as an Infrastructure implementation detail that removes real duplication.

policies.name: Unit of Work is commit boundary
policies.normalized_policy: Use IUnitOfWork as the normal commit boundary for an Application use case; repositories stage changes and Application Services decide when to commit.

policies.name: Shared UoW context and no repository container
policies.normalized_policy: Repositories in one use case share the same scoped Unit of Work/DbContext; IUnitOfWork must not become a repository container or service locator.

policies.name: Explicit transactions only for real need
policies.normalized_policy: Do not introduce explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case requires control beyond normal SaveChangesAsync.

policies.name: EF Core is Infrastructure detail
policies.normalized_policy: Use EF Core normally inside Infrastructure but do not leak EF Core concepts into Application.

policies.name: Consequential architecture changes require approval
policies.normalized_policy: Consequential choices such as Rich Domain, CQRS/MediatR/VSA, event sourcing, project-wide Result, new layers/projects, multiple DbContexts, new persistence, messaging/background infrastructure, distributed caching, microservices, auth architecture, or replacement of approved baseline technology require explicit approval.

policies.name: Constructor injection is the default
policies.normalized_policy: Use constructor injection for required dependencies by default; avoid service-locator and property-injection patterns.

policies.name: Dependency injection lifetimes must be valid
policies.normalized_policy: Respect dependency lifetimes; do not capture a shorter-lived dependency inside a longer-lived service.

policies.name: Registration stays near the owning layer
policies.normalized_policy: Keep registration close to the owning layer: Application registers Application services, Infrastructure registers persistence/adapters, and API remains the composition root.

policies.name: Cache infrastructure does not leak inward
policies.normalized_policy: Keep cache technology out of Domain and do not leak infrastructure cache APIs into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.

policies.name: Remote HTTP transport does not leak into Application
policies.normalized_policy: Infrastructure translates remote HTTP responses into Application-facing abstractions; do not leak HttpResponseMessage or remote transport concerns into Application.

policies.name: API versioning does not duplicate inner models by default
policies.normalized_policy: Do not create separate Domain or persistence models merely because the external API has multiple versions; isolate version-specific transport contracts at the API boundary when practical.

policies.name: Physical structure follows actual responsibilities
policies.normalized_policy: Do not create speculative projects, infrastructure, empty directory trees, or generic Common/Helpers/Utils buckets solely to make the repository look architectural.

policygroups.name: Persistence & Data
policygroups.description: EF Core persistence behavior, development seeding, migration/seeding separation, data lifecycle.

policies.name: Development seeding defaults to representative data
policies.normalized_policy: For an empty Development database, maintain a small deterministic representative seed dataset covering meaningful states and relationships.

policies.name: Seeding is Infrastructure/bootstrap concern
policies.normalized_policy: Development seeding belongs to Infrastructure/bootstrap and may use AppDbContext directly; it need not use Application repositories or IUnitOfWork.

policies.name: Seeder is dedicated and internal
policies.normalized_policy: Keep substantial seed construction in a dedicated internal DbSeeder/Infrastructure initialization surface, not Program.cs, DbContext configuration, entity configurations, or migrations.

policies.name: Seeding is Development-only
policies.normalized_policy: Automatic development seeding runs only in Development; never automatically seed Production; tests own their own setup.

policies.name: Seeder does not migrate schema
policies.normalized_policy: The development seeder must not call Database.Migrate(), EnsureCreated(), or otherwise create/upgrade schema; migrations are applied separately before seeding.

policies.name: Existing Development data is not auto-synchronized
policies.normalized_policy: If representative data already exists, leave it unchanged; do not use the seeder as automatic synchronization, repair, upgrade, overwrite, or recreation of an existing Development database.

policies.name: Seed data preserves domain validity
policies.normalized_policy: Seed entities must preserve current Domain invariants and valid relationships; prefer readable deterministic examples over exhaustive/random combinations.

policies.name: Seeder co-changes with model
policies.normalized_policy: Whenever Domain or persistence changes affect seeded entities, update the maintained development seeder in the same change.

policygroups.name: API, Errors & Validation
policygroups.description: HTTP semantics, error contracts, validation ownership, expected outcomes and exception policy.

policies.name: HTTP semantics belong to API
policies.normalized_policy: HTTP status codes and transport response semantics belong to the API layer; Application/Domain must not return IActionResult or ASP.NET Core status codes.

policies.name: Use structured error contracts
policies.normalized_policy: Use ProblemDetails for non-validation HTTP failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request validation; keep machine-readable contracts stable and safe.

policies.name: Use semantic success statuses
policies.normalized_policy: Choose 200/201/202/204 according to actual HTTP semantics; do not return 200 for every outcome, 201 merely for an internal row insert, or 202 for already-completed work.

policies.name: Empty collections return success
policies.normalized_policy: A successful collection query with zero matches normally returns 200 with an empty collection, not 404.

policies.name: 401/403 semantics
policies.normalized_policy: Use 401 when authentication is missing/failed and 403 when an authenticated principal is not permitted; deliberate 404 hiding requires a consistent security policy.

policies.name: Conflict and precondition semantics
policies.normalized_policy: Use 409 for valid requests conflicting with current state; use 412 when an explicit HTTP precondition such as If-Match fails.

policies.name: Unexpected exceptions handled centrally
policies.normalized_policy: Unexpected failures normally propagate to centralized IExceptionHandler handling; avoid repetitive catch/log/rethrow blocks.

policies.name: Do not leak failure internals
policies.normalized_policy: Do not expose stack traces, SQL details, connection strings, internal paths, secret values, or sensitive exception details in public API errors.

policies.name: Expected outcomes are not system failures
policies.normalized_policy: Represent common expected outcomes explicitly when useful, but do not force a generic Result<T> pattern or use HTTP-named outcome categories in Application.

policies.name: Validation stays at owning boundary
policies.normalized_policy: Use FluentValidation for explicit request/use-case validation where appropriate; keep transport validation, Application rules and Domain invariants at their owning boundaries.

policies.name: Exceptions are not normal branch control
policies.normalized_policy: Do not establish business exceptions as the default architecture or throw/catch exceptions merely to jump between normal expected branches.

policies.name: Log unexpected exceptions once
policies.normalized_policy: Unexpected exceptions should normally be logged once at the boundary that handles them; do not repeatedly log the same exception across repository, application, controller and global handler.

policies.name: API versioning is introduced only for a real compatibility need
policies.normalized_policy: Do not introduce API versioning merely because an API exists; add it when published compatibility or coexistence of client generations creates a concrete need.

policies.name: Published breaking API changes require compatibility treatment
policies.normalized_policy: Once an API version is relied on by external clients, avoid silent breaking changes; a breaking contract change normally requires a new version or another explicitly approved compatibility strategy.

policies.name: Use one explicit API versioning strategy consistently
policies.normalized_policy: When explicit API versioning is required, use one strategy consistently; URL-segment versioning is the default unless project requirements justify another strategy.

policies.name: Swagger documentation must match runtime behavior
policies.normalized_policy: Swagger/OpenAPI metadata must describe the API that actually runs, including routes, important response statuses, schemas, and authentication behavior; do not document speculative responses.

policies.name: Swagger UI exposure is environment-aware
policies.normalized_policy: Enable Swagger UI in Development by default and expose it elsewhere only when deployment requirements explicitly justify it.

policies.name: Health checks are cheap and deterministic
policies.normalized_policy: Health checks must remain cheap and deterministic and must not become full business workflows or perform expensive/mutating database work.

policies.name: Liveness and readiness have distinct dependency semantics
policies.normalized_policy: Liveness should normally avoid external dependencies that could cause restart loops; readiness may depend on capabilities required to serve traffic and should reflect startup/dependency availability appropriately.

policies.name: Public health responses do not expose internals
policies.normalized_policy: Do not expose secrets, credentials, connection details, stack traces, or unnecessary internal diagnostics through publicly reachable health responses.

policygroups.name: Testing & Quality
policygroups.description: Test strategy, isolation, readability, regression coverage and preservation of behavioral verification.

policies.name: NUnit is default backend test framework
policies.normalized_policy: Use NUnit as the default .NET automated test framework; do not introduce a second framework without a concrete reason.

policies.name: Choose narrowest useful test level
policies.normalized_policy: Choose the narrowest test level that meaningfully verifies the behavior; use integration tests when framework/persistence/HTTP wiring is the subject; no fixed unit/integration ratio is required.

policies.name: Test behavior, not implementation details
policies.normalized_policy: Tests should verify observable behavior and normally survive internal refactoring; avoid testing private calls or reproducing implementation algorithms.

policies.name: Tests are deterministic and isolated
policies.normalized_policy: Tests must be deterministic, independent of execution order, and isolated from Production/Development data, uncontrolled external systems and shared mutable state.

policies.name: Prefer explicit test cases
policies.normalized_policy: For small finite input/state spaces, prefer explicit declarative cases over loops, branching, LINQ or generated case machinery inside tests.

policies.name: Use integration tests for real composition
policies.normalized_policy: Use WebApplicationFactory-based integration testing when routing, binding, middleware, auth, DI, repositories, EF Core or database persistence is what the test must prove.

policies.name: Use provider fidelity when it matters
policies.normalized_policy: Use the actual database provider when relational/provider behavior matters; Testcontainers is optional, and do not claim provider fidelity from a different provider.

policies.name: Test data is known and owned by tests
policies.normalized_policy: Tests start from a known state and own their setup; do not depend on development seeding or execution order.

policies.name: Meaningful bugs get regression coverage
policies.normalized_policy: For a meaningful bug with plausible recurrence, add a regression test unless equivalent coverage already exists.

policies.name: Behavioral probes become maintained tests
policies.normalized_policy: If an ad-hoc/manual behavioral probe uniquely demonstrates behavior, preserve that behavior in maintained automated coverage before completion unless equivalent coverage already exists.

policies.name: Do not chase coverage percentage
policies.normalized_policy: Do not generate low-value tests merely to increase coverage percentage.

policies.name: Descriptive test naming
policies.normalized_policy: Use descriptive test names that communicate scenario/condition and expected behavior.

policygroups.name: Security
policygroups.description: Secrets, trust boundaries, SQL safety, authorization, transport security, CORS and sensitive data.

policies.name: Never commit real secrets
policies.normalized_policy: Never hardcode or commit real secrets, credentials, private keys, access/refresh tokens, or production connection strings.

policies.name: Use appropriate secret mechanisms
policies.normalized_policy: Use appropriate local secret mechanisms for development and environment-specific injection/managed secret storage for deployed environments; do not assume a cloud provider.

policies.name: Treat external data as untrusted
policies.normalized_policy: Treat data crossing the trusted boundary as untrusted and validate it at the owning layer when assumptions matter.

policies.name: Parameterize database access
policies.normalized_policy: Use parameterized database access; never build SQL by concatenating untrusted input.

policies.name: Server authorization is authoritative
policies.normalized_policy: Enforce authorization on the server; frontend route guards, hidden buttons and client checks are UX, not a security boundary.

policies.name: Anonymous access is deliberate
policies.normalized_policy: Anonymous access must be deliberate and visible; avoid redundant authorization attributes when a secure global policy already expresses intent.

policies.name: Protect sensitive transport
policies.normalized_policy: Production traffic carrying credentials or sensitive data must use TLS; respect actual hosting topology and never disable certificate validation to make integration work.

policies.name: Use reviewed cryptography/platform mechanisms
policies.normalized_policy: Do not implement custom cryptography when a well-reviewed platform mechanism is appropriate; do not treat ASP.NET Core Data Protection as universal database encryption.

policies.name: CORS is least-permissive for requirements
policies.normalized_policy: Configure CORS to the narrowest policy that satisfies actual browser-client requirements; never combine credentialed cross-origin requests with unrestricted origins.

policies.name: Do not log sensitive secrets
policies.normalized_policy: Never log passwords, tokens, private keys, auth secrets or full payment credentials; avoid PII without a concrete permitted operational need.

policies.name: Cookie auth requires CSRF consideration
policies.normalized_policy: When browser cookies automatically carry authentication credentials, include CSRF protection in the design; do not assume an Angular frontend removes the risk.

policies.name: Token storage is threat-model dependent
policies.normalized_policy: Do not claim one browser token-storage mechanism is universally secure; choose storage according to the application's threat model and never log tokens.

policies.name: Security-sensitive checks fail safely
policies.normalized_policy: Security-sensitive authorization, permission, or required-control checks should fail safely rather than silently convert lookup/configuration failures into success.

policies.name: Required security configuration fails visibly
policies.normalized_policy: When a required security control cannot be configured correctly, prefer visible startup/configuration failure over insecure fallback.

policies.name: Untrusted upload metadata is not authoritative
policies.normalized_policy: Do not trust client-provided file metadata such as MIME type as authoritative when upload handling or security decisions depend on actual content.

policygroups.name: Runtime, Code & Performance
policygroups.description: C# conventions, async/cancellation, time, outbound HTTP, caching and measured optimization.

policies.name: Correctness and clarity before optimization
policies.normalized_policy: Prefer clear correct code first; do not introduce specialized optimizations without a concrete reason and prefer measurement/profiling for non-trivial optimization.

policies.name: Use async I/O without sync-over-async
policies.normalized_policy: Use async APIs for asynchronous I/O and do not block them with .Result, .Wait(), or similar sync-over-async patterns.

policies.name: Propagate cancellation when meaningful
policies.normalized_policy: Propagate CancellationToken through asynchronous operations when cancellation is meaningful; do not add cancellation parameters to purely synchronous code without a use case.

policies.name: Use TimeProvider for testable current-time logic
policies.normalized_policy: Use TimeProvider for application logic that depends on the current clock and needs deterministic testing; do not mechanically replace explicit/stored timestamps.

policies.name: Use managed outbound HttpClient lifetime
policies.normalized_policy: Do not create/dispose a new HttpClient per request; use IHttpClientFactory or another appropriate long-lived strategy.

policies.name: Database access is efficient by default
policies.normalized_policy: Filter/project in the database when practical, avoid unnecessary round trips/over-fetching/N+1 patterns, and paginate potentially large result sets.

policies.name: Caching requires concrete semantics/need
policies.normalized_policy: Caching is not a default architecture requirement; introduce it only for a clear measured/reasoned need and choose implementation according to deployment, consistency and staleness requirements.

policies.name: Advanced optimizations require evidence
policies.normalized_policy: Compiled queries, ValueTask, pooling, custom serialization, aggressive caching and raw SQL should normally be introduced only for a measured or clearly demonstrated need.

policies.name: Follow existing C# conventions
policies.normalized_policy: Follow repository conventions and .editorconfig; use modern C# when it improves clarity, but do not mechanically modernize working code.

policies.name: Changed C# files have clean imports
policies.normalized_policy: For C# files created or modified by the task, remove unused/redundant usings while avoiding unrelated repository-wide cleanup.

policies.name: No unrelated style rewrites
policies.normalized_policy: Do not perform style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked.

policies.name: Performance changes preserve behavior
policies.normalized_policy: A performance-motivated change identifies the bottleneck, preserves behavior, uses the simplest effective optimization, maintains tests, and benchmarks/profiles non-obvious complex optimizations.

policies.name: Use structured logging with stable properties
policies.normalized_policy: Use ILogger<T> with structured message templates and stable property names; avoid string interpolation that turns structured values into opaque text.

policies.name: Do not log arbitrary payloads by default
policies.normalized_policy: Do not serialize arbitrary request bodies, domain objects, or sensitive payloads into logs by default; log the minimum operationally useful non-sensitive context.

policies.name: Outbound dependency calls have bounded execution time
policies.normalized_policy: External I/O calls must have a bounded execution time appropriate to the operation; avoid overlapping timeout mechanisms whose combined behavior is unclear.

policies.name: Retries require safe repeat semantics
policies.normalized_policy: Retry only when repeating the operation is safe; do not automatically retry state-changing operations without idempotency or another concrete safety mechanism.

policies.name: Respect server retry guidance
policies.normalized_policy: When a dependency supplies Retry-After or equivalent rate-limit guidance, respect it where appropriate and do not retry indefinitely or aggressively.

policies.name: Fallback must preserve acceptable semantics
policies.normalized_policy: Use fallback only when the fallback result is semantically acceptable; do not hide correctness failures behind convenient default values.

policies.name: Caller cancellation is not a transient failure
policies.normalized_policy: Do not classify caller cancellation as a transient dependency failure or convert it into repeated outbound attempts.

policies.name: Cache keys identify the cached value safely
policies.normalized_policy: Cache keys must uniquely represent the cached value and include relevant user/tenant/context dimensions; avoid global keys for user- or tenant-specific data.

policies.name: Cache invalidation follows committed mutation semantics
policies.normalized_policy: Invalidate/update cache entries only in a way consistent with successful underlying mutations; do not make cache state a second source of truth.

policies.name: Structured configuration uses typed options
policies.normalized_policy: Prefer strongly typed options for structured service configuration and validate settings at startup when missing/invalid values prevent correct or secure operation; avoid scattering string-based IConfiguration lookups.

policygroups.name: Dependencies & Technology Stack
policygroups.description: Dependency governance and approved/default technology choices.

policies.name: Dependencies require current need
policies.normalized_policy: Add a dependency only for a concrete current requirement; do not install packages for hypothetical future use.

policies.name: Approved technology is not silently replaced
policies.normalized_policy: When the template/project has an approved technology, use it rather than silently selecting an alternative; consequential replacement requires approval.

policies.name: Choose latest stable compatible version
policies.normalized_policy: For NuGet/npm additions or updates, verify the current latest stable compatible version from the registry; avoid prerelease and floating versions unless explicitly requested.

policies.name: Dependency due diligence
policies.normalized_policy: Before installation, check deprecation, known vulnerabilities and the exact selected version's license.

policies.name: Commercial/risky licenses require approval
policies.normalized_policy: Do not automatically install paid/commercial or materially restrictive/unclear-license dependencies; explain the concern and reasonable alternatives without silently substituting.

policies.name: Central Package Management
policies.normalized_policy: Use NuGet Central Package Management; versions belong in Directory.Packages.props and project PackageReference entries are normally versionless and narrowly scoped.

policies.name: npm lockfile and dependency category
policies.normalized_policy: Use npm by default unless deliberately changed, keep package-lock consistent, and place build/test tooling in the appropriate dependency category.

policies.name: Default backend platform
policies.normalized_policy: Default platform is .NET 10 LTS, C# 14, ASP.NET Core and ASP.NET Core Controllers; do not move to preview/RC without approval.

policies.name: Default persistence stack
policies.normalized_policy: Default persistence is EF Core with Microsoft SQL Server/SqlServer provider; provider-specific concerns stay out of Application and Domain.

policies.name: Default validation/logging
policies.normalized_policy: FluentValidation is the standard explicit request/use-case validation library; application logging uses ILogger<T> with Serilog as provider.

policies.name: Conditional mapping/resilience
policies.normalized_policy: Manual mapping is fine for simple cases; Mapster is approved when mapping volume warrants it. Microsoft resilience packages are approved only when real integrations need resilience.

policies.name: Swagger baseline
policies.normalized_policy: Use Swashbuckle Swagger UI as the default Development interactive API documentation/testing surface; expose outside Development only when requirements justify it.

policies.name: Backend testing stack/layout
policies.normalized_policy: Use NUnit; backend test projects live under backend alongside production projects; WebApplicationFactory is the baseline for ASP.NET Core integration tests; Testcontainers is conditional.

policies.name: Angular baseline stack
policies.normalized_policy: Use current stable Angular with compatible TypeScript/RxJS, standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, zoneless mode when supported, SCSS, Angular Material/CDK and Vitest.

policies.name: Avoid overlapping Angular libraries by default
policies.normalized_policy: Do not add NgRx, Axios, Lodash, Bootstrap, Tailwind, extra form/component/state libraries by default; use built-in Angular capabilities first and add extras only for concrete needs.

policies.name: Conditional E2E
policies.normalized_policy: Playwright is the approved default when frontend E2E coverage is required, but it is not part of the minimal baseline scaffold.

policies.name: API versioning package is conditional
policies.normalized_policy: When Controller API versioning is explicitly adopted, use the Controller integration of Asp.Versioning; do not add the package before the project actually adopts versioning.

policies.name: Docker is optional infrastructure
policies.normalized_policy: Do not introduce Docker merely because the application can be containerized; add container artifacts only when the project or deployment actually needs them.

policies.name: Production containers use an appropriate runtime image
policies.normalized_policy: For production containers, use an appropriate runtime image rather than the SDK image solely for convenience, and avoid switching to root merely to bypass filesystem problems.

policies.name: Modern Microsoft resilience integration is the default
policies.normalized_policy: When resilience is required, prefer Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience for HttpClient and Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience for general pipelines; direct Polly integration is an explicit exception rather than the default.

policies.name: Modern Serilog integration is the baseline
policies.normalized_policy: When Serilog is configured, use the modern DI-integrated AddSerilog approach and keep provider configuration in environment-aware configuration; application code continues to depend on ILogger<T>.

policies.name: Use current solution format by default
policies.normalized_policy: For the current .NET template use the .slnx solution format by default; use legacy .sln only when an external tool or project requirement requires it.

policies.name: Shared .NET build/package configuration is repository-level
policies.normalized_policy: Use repository-level Directory.Build.props for genuinely shared .NET build settings and Directory.Packages.props for Central Package Management; keep project-specific settings in their owning projects.

policies.name: Default physical solution layout remains explicit
policies.normalized_policy: Keep backend production/test projects, frontend workspace, and documentation clearly separated according to the template's approved layout; do not create a separate top-level tests directory.

policygroups.name: Frontend
policygroups.description: Angular structure, state, HTTP boundary, routing, forms, frontend security and error handling.

policies.name: Modern standalone Angular
policies.normalized_policy: Use modern standalone Angular APIs for new code and organize application code primarily by feature.

policies.name: Presentation stays focused
policies.normalized_policy: Keep pages/components focused on presentation and UI orchestration; do not move trivial presentation logic into services merely to shrink components.

policies.name: Explicit frontend HTTP boundary
policies.normalized_policy: Keep backend communication in explicit feature data-access/services; do not scatter HttpClient calls through presentation components or import backend Domain entities into Angular.

policies.name: Signals vs RxJS by semantics
policies.normalized_policy: Use Signals for naturally synchronous/local UI state and RxJS when asynchronous streams, HTTP composition, cancellation or event pipelines are clearer; avoid mechanical conversions.

policies.name: Lazy-load meaningful features
policies.normalized_policy: Use route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; do not lazy-load every tiny component.

policies.name: Prefer simple local state
policies.normalized_policy: Prefer simple local/component/service state before introducing a state-management library.

policies.name: Frontend structure stays feature-oriented
policies.normalized_policy: Avoid application-wide technical buckets and empty architecture folders; keep feature-specific code within the feature and keep core/shared relatively small.

policies.name: Functional interceptors are cross-cutting
policies.normalized_policy: Prefer functional interceptors for new code and keep interceptor responsibilities cross-cutting; do not put feature business logic in interceptors.

policies.name: Frontend understands documented API errors
policies.normalized_policy: Frontend code follows the documented API error contract; centralize reusable ProblemDetails parsing when practical and do not infer business behavior from arbitrary human-readable exception messages.

policies.name: Frontend validation is UX, backend remains authoritative
policies.normalized_policy: Use reactive forms for non-trivial forms when useful; frontend validation improves UX but does not replace backend validation or data-integrity/security enforcement.

policygroups.name: Workflows & Delivery
policygroups.description: Review, verification, completion, reporting and workflow behavior.

policies.name: Inspect existing code before non-trivial change
policies.normalized_policy: Inspect relevant existing code before making non-trivial changes and apply applicable rules/skills.

policies.name: Review substantial work before final verification
policies.normalized_policy: For substantial feature work or a newly implemented application, run the code-review workflow before final verify.

policies.name: Verification required before completion
policies.normalized_policy: Before declaring implementation complete, run the verify workflow appropriate to the scope and risk.

policies.name: Verification starts with final diff/scope
policies.normalized_policy: Review the final changed-file set/diff, confirm scope, remove accidental artifacts/secrets, and determine affected repository areas before choosing checks.

policies.name: Build/test affected areas externally
policies.normalized_policy: Build affected projects and run relevant tests; a build failure means implementation is not complete and new relevant failures must be investigated.

policies.name: Runtime smoke for substantial composition changes
policies.normalized_policy: For new runnable applications or substantial startup/configuration/persistence/full-stack changes, verify intended Development startup and key composition surfaces.

policies.name: Architecture/security/dependency checks are risk-scoped
policies.normalized_policy: Run architecture, formatting/analyzer, dependency and security checks when relevant to the change rather than indiscriminately.

policies.name: Fix and retry until green or blocked
policies.normalized_policy: When verification fails, make the smallest appropriate fix and rerun affected checks until green or genuine user input is required; do not hide known failures.

policies.name: Report actual verification state
policies.normalized_policy: Report what was actually run using PASS/NOT RUN/NOT APPLICABLE; never imply an unchecked area passed.

policies.name: Code reviewer is independent and read-only
policies.normalized_policy: The code-reviewer performs an independent read-only review and uses code-review as the canonical procedure rather than redefining policy.

policies.name: Review prioritizes defects over style
policies.normalized_policy: Prioritize correctness, security, data integrity, architecture, concurrency/integration, meaningful tests, maintainability and credible performance; do not elevate style preferences above defects.

policies.name: Do not manufacture review findings
policies.normalized_policy: Do not invent findings to populate categories; when no meaningful findings exist, say so and state important unverifiable areas.

policies.name: Build-fix starts from reproduction and diagnosis
policies.normalized_policy: When repairing a build/test failure, reproduce and diagnose the actual failure before editing; fix root causes before downstream symptoms.

policies.name: Build-fix uses focused bounded iteration
policies.normalized_policy: Use small bounded repair iterations, rerun the narrowest failing verification after meaningful fixes, and expand verification only after the focused failure is resolved.

policies.name: Do not weaken verification to make it pass
policies.normalized_policy: Do not weaken, delete, skip, or suppress relevant tests/compiler/analyzer failures merely to make verification pass.

policies.name: Fix generated outputs at their source
policies.normalized_policy: When generated output is wrong, prefer fixing its source configuration/input and regenerating; do not patch disposable generated output unless the repository intentionally treats it as maintained source.

policies.name: CI reproduces supported build/test commands and keeps failures visible
policies.normalized_policy: CI definitions stay in source control, reproduce the repository's supported build/test commands, and must not hide build/test failures.

policies.name: CI uses repository-declared frontend commands and lockfile
policies.normalized_policy: In CI, use scripts that actually exist and use npm ci when a maintained lockfile supports it; do not invent npm scripts or reflexively replace lockfile-based installs.

policies.name: Production migrations are deliberate deployment work
policies.normalized_policy: Do not automatically apply production database migrations from normal application startup by default; treat production migration as an explicit deployment operation using approved credentials and never run Development seeding in Production.

policies.name: Security findings require evidence and contextual severity
policies.normalized_policy: Security review must distinguish confirmed findings from items needing verification and assign severity from exploitability, reachability, impact, and application context rather than suspicious patterns or raw CVSS alone.

policies.name: Security review cannot depend on one scanner
policies.normalized_policy: Do not require a specific MCP server, analyzer, commercial scanner, or external tool for security review to work; use available tooling as evidence, not as the sole authority.

policies.name: Git commits and staging remain focused
policies.normalized_policy: Before committing, inspect the staged diff and include only the logical requested change; do not stage or clean unrelated modified files.

coverage_policy.includes: Stable normative statements, defaults, prohibitions, approved technology decisions, approval gates, and workflow obligations whose loss or semantic drift would change candidate behavior.
coverage_policy.excludes: Pure examples, explanatory prose, code samples, optional technique, troubleshooting detail, and private knowledge that does not itself impose a normative requirement.
coverage_policy.source_file_coverage_rule: A V2 file may legitimately have zero inventory references when it contains knowledge/examples only. A normative statement must either map to an inventory policy or be intentionally classified as non-oracle material.
coverage_policy.validation_usage: After candidate generation, compare candidate runtime instructions to this oracle for missing owners, duplicate owners, semantic weakening/strengthening, and unapproved additional normative policy.
